articles.title: NHRC seeks Education Ministry’s response over alleged neglect of Veer Baal Diwas in schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The NHRC acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh

National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) on Friday sought an explanation from the Union Ministry of Education over allegations that schools across the country give greater prominence to Children’s Day celebrations on November 14 while failing to adequately highlight the historical significance of Veer Baal Diwas, observed on December 26.

The Commission’s bench, headed by member Priyank Kanoongo, acted on a complaint submitted by Sanjeev Newar of the Seva Nyay Utthan Foundation, which raised concerns about the limited awareness among school students regarding the courage and supreme sacrifice of the four Sahibzadas of Guru Gobind Singh.

The Commission hence issued a notice to the Secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education, Government of India asking whether the Central Government or any competent authority has issued an official notification, order or circular declaring November 14 as Children’s Day. If such a directive exists, the Ministry has been asked to furnish a copy and provide the relevant details.
The Ministry has been directed to submit a detailed Action Taken Report (ATR) within 14 days, addressing the concerns raised in the complaint.

The NHRC has also sought clarification on whether schools are being encouraged to conduct dedicated educational and awareness programmes on December 26 to commemorate Veer Baal Diwas. Such initiatives, the Commission has indicated, should help students understand the historical significance of the four Sahibzadas and their extraordinary courage and sacrifice.

Highlighting the broader educational implications of the issue, the Commission stressed the need to ensure that children are exposed to important chapters of India’s history and cultural heritage. It observed that educational institutions play a significant role in nurturing awareness of values such as bravery, faith, sacrifice and resistance to injustice.

articles.title: The challenge of holding the Quad together
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The big ticket question confronting the Quad, however, is how Donald Trump engages with the group and the broader Indo-Pacific geography

Speaking to the media on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, the U.S. Secretary of State announced that the leaders of the four Quad countries — India, Australia, Japan and the U.S. — are expected to meet in Manila in November, on the sidelines of the ASEAN Summit. The announcement is significant, as this would be the first summit-level meeting of the Quad leaders since Donald Trump began his second term as U.S. President. It would also be the first such summit attended by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi since she assumed office. The last Quad Leaders’ Summit was held in Wilmington in 2024, when Joe Biden was U.S. President and Fumio Kishida was Japan’s Prime Minister.

While India was expected to host the subsequent Quad Leaders’ Summit, the grouping underwent a period of intense strategic turbulence in 2025, on account of Washington’s shifting geopolitical priorities and changing political dynamics in its bilateral relations with Quad members, especially India. However, this did not result in complete collapse of the grouping. Apart from the leader-level summit, the group has remained successful in continuing its operational synergies in its various initiatives. This was most evident in the elevation of the Quad’s Indo-Pacific Maritime Domain Awareness initiative to the Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration framework, launched in New Delhi in May 2026, following the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting.
Political & National Report: The challenge of holding the Quad together. This development is a key milestone in India's ongoing legislative, judicial, and constitutional governance framework.

articles.title: Comply with new prices of 137 anti-cancer drugs or face action, says regulator
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: NPPA directs State drug controllers to strictly monitor prices
The National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) has warned of penal action against those failing to comply with the revised prices of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs

The authority, which functions under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, has asked State drug controllers (SDCs) to strictly monitor the prices and submit their action taken reports by November 16, according to an official release on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The revised prices for the 137 anti-cancer drugs came into effect on November 9, 2026, following a gazette order issued on October 17, 2026. The order capped the trade margin on these medicines at 30%.

Based on submissions received from pharmaceutical companies up to November 11, the latest revised price lists have been uploaded on the NPPA website as well as the Pharma Sahi Daam app and portal, the Chemicals and Fertilizers Ministry said.

All manufacturers, stockists, dealers, retailers, hospitals, and medical institutions have been directed to comply with the revised prices and prominently display the updated price lists at their premises and on their websites.

The SDCs have been instructed to strictly monitor compliance across the supply chain and healthcare facilities to ensure that the benefits of the revised maximum retail prices (MRPs) are passed on to patients.
Any violation of the directive may attract overcharging proceedings under the provisions of the DPCO, 2013, the release noted.

Complaints regarding overcharging, shortage, or non-availability of medicines can be reported through the Pharma Sahi Daam app or portal, the NPPA helpline (1800-111-255), or via email at monitoring-nppa@gov.in, it added.

articles.title: Andhra Pradesh secures ₹9.88 lakh crore investment commitments at CII Partnership Summit in Vizag
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: A.P. government will implement Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024, says Chief Minister Naidu

The Andhra Pradesh government would implement the Investment Protection Act with retrospective effect from 2024 and initiate the provision of clearances to industries in real time based on self-certification to encourage investors, Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has said, adding that the proposed law would be passed in the coming session of the Legislative Assembly.

Addressing the media after the valedictory of the 31st CII Partnership Summit here on Friday, Mr. Naidu said there was a pressing need for good governance and that investors needed to be reassured about the safety of their investments in the event of a regime change. This was “keeping in view the ruin caused between 2019 and 2024”, which aggravated the impact of State bifurcation.

The government would be liberal in facilitating businesses, but not be lenient in ensuring accountability for the support being availed, Mr. Naidu said, noting that while mobilising investments with due sense of urgency, it was ensuring that they would take tangible shape as per the committed timelines.

Besides, the compliance burden was being reduced to make doing business far more easier. Due focus was being laid on making the agriculture sector resilient, as the government could not afford to lay the whole emphasis on the industrial sector only. Both sectors are crucial to increase the Gross State Domestic Product, he said.

The Chief Minister said that the State attracted investments of nearly ₹9.88 lakh crore through 303 MoUs during the current edition of the CII Partnership Summit and that they have the potential to generate approximately 3.49 lakh jobs across sectors. The cumulative investments that have been tied up since June 2024 have reached ₹32.49 lakh crore.
“Andhra Pradesh is hogging the limelight, with its distinct advantages for investors and the potential of the three economic regions of Amaravati, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam,” he said.

The government was extending all possible support for businesses in emerging sectors to thrive, and a priority has been accorded to development of the space sector around India’s only spaceport at Sriharikota, he said.

Union Civil Aviation Minister K. Rammohan Naidu; MPs T. Krishna Prasad and M. Sribharat; Ministers T.G. Bharat, K. Atchannaidu, P. Narayana, Kollu Ravindra, Kondapalli Srinivas, Kolusu Parthasarathy and Satya Kumar Yadav were present.

Chandrababu Naidu has said, adding that the proposed law would be passed in the coming session of the Legislative Assembly.

Addressing the media after the valedictory of the 31st CII Partnership Summit here on Friday, Mr. Naidu said there was a pressing need for good governance and that investors needed to be reassured about the safety of their investments in the event of a regime change. This was “keeping in view the ruin caused between 2019 and 2024”, which aggravated the impact of State bifurcation.

The government would be liberal in facilitating businesses, but not be lenient in ensuring accountability for the support being availed, Mr. Naidu said, noting that while mobilising investments with due sense of urgency, it was ensuring that they would take tangible shape as per the committed timelines.

Besides, the compliance burden was being reduced to make doing business far more easier. Due focus was being laid on making the agriculture sector resilient, as the government could not afford to lay the whole emphasis on the industrial sector only. Both sectors are crucial to increase the Gross State Domestic Product, he said.

The Chief Minister said that the State attracted investments of nearly ₹9.88 lakh crore through 303 MoUs during the current edition of the CII Partnership Summit and that they have the potential to generate approximately 3.49 lakh jobs across sectors. The cumulative investments that have been tied up since June 2024 have reached ₹32.49 lakh crore.

“Andhra Pradesh is hogging the limelight, with its distinct advantages for investors and the potential of the three economic regions of Amaravati, Tirupati and Visakhapatnam,” he said.

The government was extending all possible support for businesses in emerging sectors to thrive, and a priority has been accorded to development of the space sector around India’s only spaceport at Sriharikota, he said.

articles.title: Tanker hits a river cruise boat on Mississippi River in New Orleans; rescue operations under way
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Authorities did not immediately release whether there were injuries or deaths; video from the scene showed the much larger Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the paddlewheel cruise boat while it appeared to be docked as metal and glass crashed and crunched

A tanker struck the American Heritage river cruise paddleboat in New Orleans on Friday (November 13, 2026) with 129 passengers aboard, partially submerging the boat. Rescues were under way on the Mississippi River, officials said.
Authorities did not immediately release whether there were injuries or deaths.
Video from the scene showed the much larger Atlantic Asphalt tanker hit the paddlewheel cruise boat while it appeared to be docked as metal and glass crashed and crunched.

More than a dozen people in lifejackets were being dragged from the 19°C river onto nearby ships. Others were standing near the railing as the other side of the American Heritage listed further into the water.
“Surreal — that’s what that was,” witness Jamie Holford told WDSU-TV . “Fifteen minutes from impact to where it rolled over.”
The cruise ship was built in 2015 and operated by American Cruise Lines. It is five stories and can hold up to 150 passengers.
The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to several Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi.

The tanker involved in the crash specialises in carrying large quantities of asphalt and bitumen, a semi-solid substance that is often used for road construction and roofing, according to the live shipping tracker MarineTraffic.

Ships carrying asphalt and bitumen are often heated well above 120°C to prevent the asphalt from solidifying on the ship, according to the maritime periodical Marine Insights. It is not immediately clear whether the ship was carrying any materials when the crash occurred.
The 160-metre long vessel had a final destination in New Orleans, according to MarineTraffic, and was sailing under a flag for the Marshall Islands.

articles.title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security

Urgent pleas for cash from poor ​nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye’s COP31 talks as Western governments put ‌national security and living costs first.

Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple ​climate funding for poorer countries to $300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target. Also by 2035, financing ⁠from all public and private sources combined would be $1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.

Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as U.S. President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and West Asia have added to inflationary ‌pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.

“Like many small island ‌developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode,” Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. “We cannot build resilience ‌while ⁠our fiscal space erodes.”
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of ⁠small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.

Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on ​domestic bus fares.
The Stockholm ‌International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) estimated in April that world military expenditure reached $2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9% in real terms from 2024.

Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.

fullParagraphs: Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow, a statement from the Turkish presidency quoted President Erdogan as saying

“President Erdogan stated that we ‌would continue working together to prevent the resurgence of war in ‌the Gulf region and establish a ‌basis ⁠for dialogue and achieve peace,” ⁠the presidency said in a statement on X, which did not provide details on the defence accord.
The ​statement cited ‌him as saying that Turkiye and Qatar were working to develop and diversify their energy partnership, and that their cooperation ‌in the defence industry would ​continue to grow.
“President Erdogan stated that the Mutual Defence Agreement signed today ⁠by Turkey and Qatar would add another dimension to our brotherhood,” it added.
In August, ‌Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca, bringing together the Sunni Muslim U.S. allies at a time of conflict across the region.

Turkiye’s parliament ratified the ‌so-called Mecca Joint Defence Agreement last week, clearing ​the way for Ankara to send military support to Saudi Arabia, which ⁠has been struggling to fend off attacks ⁠by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi militants.
Under the agreement, signed by the three ‌regional powers in August, an attack on one party constitutes an attack ​on all.

In its latest update on Friday (November 13, 2026), the company said it was making progress in fixing the outage, which has affected email access and workplace applications in businesses, public services, and other organisations across the globe. In India, the disruptions affected businesses from startups to multinational corporations.

A senior executive at a major telecom company in India told The Hindu that employees were unable to access emails or send service-disruption alerts to customers. Call-centre traffic also increased, the executive said.

Rahul Ganapathy, co-founder and CEO of deep tech startup Atsuya Technologies, said customer emails and scheduled Teams meetings were disrupted, although his company did not rely entirely on Microsoft internally.
At a Big Four professional services firm in Bengaluru, a senior employee said its internal operations were affected, but added that IT teams were restoring services.
The disruptions also left airlines experiencing customer-support delays.

IndiGo said its email support was affected and advised customers to use 6E Skai, its AI-powered virtual assistant. Akasa Air warned of email support delays and directed passengers to its customer care centre and social media. Air India said flight operations were unaffected, although it rerouted emails.

Separately, India’s Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, issued a high-severity advisory on Friday, warning of multiple vulnerabilities in Microsoft products. It flagged an Outlook vulnerability that it said was being actively exploited and urged users to apply security updates. The advisory did not explicitly link the vulnerabilities to the outage.

Microsoft identified Exchange Online — described as its cloud-based messaging platform that delivers email, calendar, contacts, and tasks — as the primary service affected. Some Microsoft Graph requests accessing Exchange Online data timed out, affecting dependent features in Teams, Copilot, and SharePoint, the company said. Core Teams messaging and online meetings largely continued normally, it added.

On Friday, Microsoft said recovery was progressing, with improvements in North America and Europe and encouraging signs in Asia-Pacific. Service availability and email delivery were improving, but intermittent access problems and delays could continue, it said, adding that it was working through email backlogs and retained a 48-hour timeout window to protect delayed messages. Service health and capacity had not fully returned to baseline, it said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday (November 14, 2026) paid tribute to the country's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, on his birth anniversary.

articles.title: MP adds 8.19 lakh voters since final SIR roll, electorate rises to 5.48 crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: With the latest additions, the total number of registered electors in Madhya Pradesh stands at 5,47,99,628 — comprising 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 transgender persons

Madhya Pradesh has recorded an addition of 8.19 lakh voters in the draft electoral roll published under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, taking the state's total electorate to nearly 5.48 crore, two years ahead of the next assembly elections, officials said.

Compared with the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in February this year, the latest draft, released on Thursday (November 12, 2026), shows an addition of 4,38,361 women, 3,80,169 men and 33 transgender voters, according to Election Commission (EC) figures.
With the latest additions, the total number of registered electors in Madhya Pradesh stands at 5,47,99,628 — comprising 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 transgender persons.
The State had 5,39,81,065 voters, including 2,79,04,975 males, 2,60,75,186 females and 904 transgender persons, when the SIR list was published in February.
Age-wise data shows that the 30-39 age bracket accounts for the highest number of voters at 1,40,50,865, followed by the 20-29 age group at 1,29,48,107.
The EC has invited claims and objections till December 11, following which the final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027.
ALSO WATCH Madhya Pradesh: Over 30 tribal children die in Balaghat, many hospitalised

The increase in the number of voters assumes significance as the SIR had triggered a political row, with the Congress alleging the removal of eligible voters and the ruling BJP defending the exercise, maintaining it was undertaken to purge the names of deceased, shifted, absent and duplicate voters.
Madhya Pradesh is scheduled to go to the polls towards the end of 2028. The state's population is projected to reach 9.05 crore, compared with 7.26 crore recorded in the 2011 Census.

Madhya Pradesh has 230 assembly seats, of which 47 are reserved for Scheduled Tribes and 35 for Scheduled Castes, and 29 Lok Sabha constituencies, including six reserved for Scheduled Tribes and four for Scheduled Castes.

📰 MP adds 8.19 lakh voters since final SIR roll, electorate rises to 5.48 crore

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

With the latest additions, the total number of registered electors in Madhya Pradesh stands at 5,47,99,628 — comprising 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 transgender persons

Madhya Pradesh has recorded an addition of 8.19 lakh voters in the draft electoral roll published under the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, taking the state's total electorate to nearly 5.48 crore, two years ahead of the next assembly elections, officials said.

Compared with the final Special Intensive Revision (SIR) roll published in February this year, the latest draft, released on Thursday (November 12, 2026), shows an addition of 4,38,361 women, 3,80,169 men and 33 transgender voters, according to Election Commission (EC) figures.

With the latest additions, the total number of registered electors in Madhya Pradesh stands at 5,47,99,628 — comprising 2,82,85,144 men, 2,65,13,547 women and 937 transgender persons.

The State had 5,39,81,065 voters, including 2,79,04,975 males, 2,60,75,186 females and 904 transgender persons, when the SIR list was published in February.

Age-wise data shows that the 30-39 age bracket accounts for the highest number of voters at 1,40,50,865, followed by the 20-29 age group at 1,29,48,107.

The EC has invited claims and objections till December 11, following which the final electoral roll will be published on January 4, 2027.

ALSO WATCH Madhya Pradesh: Over 30 tribal children die in Balaghat, many hospitalised

The increase in the number of voters assumes significance as the SIR had triggered a political row, with the Congress alleging the removal of eligible voters and the ruling BJP defending the exercise, maintaining it was undertaken to purge the names of deceased, shifted, absent and duplicate voters.

Madhya Pradesh is scheduled to go to the polls towards the end of 2028. The state's population is projected to reach 9.05 crore, compared with 7.26 crore recorded in the 2011 Census.

Madhya Pradesh has 230 assembly seats, of which 47 are reserved for Scheduled Tribes and 35 for Scheduled Castes, and 29 Lok Sabha constituencies, including six reserved for Scheduled Tribes and four for Scheduled Castes.

articles.title: Driver from Theni found dead while in custody at Chekkanoorani police station in Madurai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Cargo vehicle driver from Theni, who was being questioned over some missing bags of cardamom, was found dead in the restroom; police say he ended his life

A cargo vehicle driver from Theni, Balakrishnan, who was being questioned on Friday (November 13, 2026) at Chekkanoorani police station in connection with a case of missing bags of cardamom last week, was found dead in a restroom at the police station on Saturday (November 14) morning.
The police said the driver had transported cardamom from Theni to Madurai, and on the way, a few bags of the spices had been destroyed in a fire, on November 3.

The manager of the agent who had sent the cardamom raised suspicion over some missing bags of the spice. Based on a petition given by him, the police had asked Balakrishnan, of Devaram in Theni district, to appear at the station.
After receiving a complaint from Balakrishnan over the accidental fire case, the police questioned him through Friday night.
On Saturday morning, he was found dead in the restroom on the police station premises.
The police claimed the driver said he wanted to use the restroom and was later found to have ended his life.

articles.title: Attack on Nehru 60 years after death testament to his commitment to India: Priyanka
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Paying tributes to India's first Prime Minister, the Wayanad MP said Nehru was that unique human being — a revolutionary, a visionary and a builder

Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Saturday (November 14, 2026) hailed Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary, saying the fact that he is still attacked by those who seek to destroy the Constitution and democracy more than 60 years after his death is a testament to his steadfast commitment to India.
Paying tributes to India's first Prime Minister, the Wayanad MP said Nehru was that unique human being — a revolutionary, a visionary and a builder.

"The fact that he is still attacked by those who seek to destroy our constitution and our democracy more than sixty years after his death is a testament to his steadfast commitment to India," she said on X
"May his love for our country guide us for always," she added.
Nehru was born on this day in 1889 in Allahabad (now Prayagraj).

articles.title: Rubio assails international court in speech to conservative legal group
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The U.S., Mr. Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats”

Secretary of State Marco Rubio attacked the International Criminal Court in a speech ​to a conservative legal group on Friday (November 13, 2026), arguing for a muscular foreign ⁠policy and against international law restraining U.S. actions.

Mr. Rubio’s speech to the Federalist Society in Washington, his first prepared remarks since Republicans were routed in the midterm elections on November 3 , heightens speculation over whether he ‌will leave his roles as national security adviser and top U.S. diplomat to run for president in 2028.

Mr. Rubio, who has at times sought to ‌provide an intellectual justification for President Donald Trump’s “America First” foreign policy, has firmly denied reports ‌he ⁠will soon embark on a presidential campaign, but the Federalist Society is ⁠an occasional stop for Republican hopefuls.

He has dismissed criticisms that the Trump administration has broken international law by such actions as seizing Venezuelan then-President Nicolas Maduro and striking boats in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific that it says ​were carrying drugs.

In his speech, Mr. Rubio said ‌the goal of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran was to prevent Tehran from ever developing a nuclear weapon, which he said was particularly urgent because the Islamic Republic’s “radical Shia clerics” had an “expansionist mentality.”

He contrasted this with the government of North Korea’s Kim Jong ‌Un, whom Mr. Trump has met three times. “I’m not excusing the terrible things that ​have happened there,” Rubio said of North Korea. “I’m just saying he [Kim] is not expansionist. He’s not trying to invade Japan or, you know, China ⁠or whatever.”

The U.S., Mr. Rubio said, would not “submit to the sterile vision of radical judges or soulless global bureaucrats,” repeating his assertion that the court would try to prosecute US officials or ‌service members that he used to justify sanctions against the ICC announced last month.

“Americans have never agreed to submit to the ICC’s authority, but that court and its allies in the global bureaucracy have appointed themselves judge and jury and executioner of the international order,” Mr. Rubio said.

The Trump administration has long been hostile to the Netherlands-based court, founded in 2002 to prosecute war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide, and has previously imposed sanctions on ‌its prosecutors and judges. The ICC has received strong backing from most member states, which include all EU ​countries and all members of the NATO alliance apart from the United States and Turkey.

Washington has denounced the court over arrest warrants issued for Israeli ⁠officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and an investigation into actions of US soldiers in Afghanistan, which ⁠the ICC says is “deprioritized.”

articles.title: U.S. FAA ground stop LIVE updates: Flights resume as hours-long halt lifted; Trump admin. blames ‘overloaded' systems
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Trump administration rules out foul play, Transportation Secretary says major communications outage caused by decades old technology

Tens of thousands of fliers were forced to change their plans when the FAA issued a ground stop ‌that lasted four hours and led to the cancellations of more than 6,600 flights, with 8,600 delayed, according to FlightRadar24.
It was just the third nationwide stop issued by ‌the Federal Aviation Administration this century.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the problems not on malicious actors ‌but ⁠on a failure of aging network technology in the radar and communications system used ⁠for air traffic control.

At the Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, where information displays were almost completely filled with flights marked “Delayed” or “Cancelled,” some travellers appeared resigned as they wondered how long the delays would last and how their travel plans would be affected.

NBA, NHL and college teams were left stranded as they tried to reach their destinations. Meanwhile, NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time to travel to their games this weekend.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said NCAA teams will be prioritised ahead of football games on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
“I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA, to schedule their flight times and make sure they can move” to make their kickoff, he said.
FedEx, the world’s largest cargo airline, said it was prepared to activate contingency plans to keep any possible disruptions at a minimum.

U.S. airlines move about 61,000 tons (55,340 metric tonnes) of goods — from letters to packages — to and from more than 220 countries daily, according to the industry trade group Airlines for America.
Despite the ground stop, SpaceX launched its Starship rocket from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) afternoon in its latest test flight.

articles.title: Indian envoy slams USCIRF over Sharjeel Imam remarks, says panel has 'no locus standi'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In a strongly worded post on X, Vinay Kwatra rejected the commission’s assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India’s commitment to religious freedom and equal rights

India’s Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) slammed the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) over its remarks on jailed activist Sharjeel Imam, asserting that the commission had "no locus standi" to pass judgment on the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.

In a strongly worded post on X , Mr. Kwatra rejected the commission's assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights. "USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths," Mr. Kwatra said.

USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India's constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths. India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others.

"India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others," he added.

The ambassador's remarks came after the USCIRF shared Imam's profile on X , describing him as "a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy.” The commission's post characterised Mr. Imam's detention as being linked to his advocacy for religious freedom, a description that drew a sharp response from the Indian envoy.

Sharjeel Imam, a former student activist, was arrested in January 2020 in connection with protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), which took place in December 2019 and January 2020. Authorities accused him of delivering speeches that allegedly incited communal violence. In August 2020, he was charged in connection with FIR 59/2020, relating to the larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The charges invoked provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), including those relating to rioting, murder, promoting enmity, unlawful activities and alleged terrorist acts. The case is being investigated by the Delhi Police Special Cell.

Separately, on October 10, a Delhi Court declined to entertain a Delhi Police plea seeking cancellation of Mr. Imam's seven-day interim bail, despite observing that he had apparently violated a condition restricting his interaction with the media. Additional Sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai of the Karkardooma Courts examined video footage submitted by the prosecution, which allegedly showed Imam present in a room where a media person was interviewing his brother. The prosecution contended that Mr. Imam had breached the bail conditions by coming into contact with a media person. However, his counsel denied the allegations, arguing that the footage did not establish any direct interaction between Imam and the journalist.

Imam had been granted interim bail from October 4 to October 10 to attend his cousin's wedding functions. The relief was subject to conditions prohibiting him from using social media, interacting with media persons and meeting individuals other than family members, relatives and friends. Taking note of the defence's submission that Mr. Imam had boarded a flight to Delhi and would surrender before jail authorities that evening, the Court declined to cancel his interim bail and disposed of the police application.

In a strongly worded post on X, Vinay Kwatra rejected the commission’s assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India’s commitment to religious freedom and equal rights

India’s Ambassador to the United States, Vinay Mohan Kwatra, on Saturday (November 14, 2026) slammed the United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) over its remarks on jailed activist Sharjeel Imam, asserting that the commission had "no locus standi" to pass judgment on the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.

In a strongly worded post on X , Mr. Kwatra rejected the commission's assessment, accusing it of making partisan and ill-informed observations about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights. "USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens. Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish India’s constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths," Mr. Kwatra said.

India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Sharjeel Imam, a former student activist, was arrested in January 2020 in connection with protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA), which took place in December 2019 and January 2020. Authorities accused him of delivering speeches that allegedly incited communal violence. In August 2020, he was charged in connection with FIR 59/2020, relating to the larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The charges invoked provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), including those relating to rioting, murder, promoting enmity, unlawful activities and alleged terrorist acts. The case is being investigated by the Delhi Police Special Cell.

Separately, on October 10, a Delhi Court declined to entertain a Delhi Police plea seeking cancellation of Mr. Imam's seven-day interim bail, despite observing that he had apparently violated a condition restricting his interaction with the media. Additional Sessions Judge Sameer Bajpai of the Karkardooma Courts examined video footage submitted by the prosecution, which allegedly showed Imam present in a room where a media person was interviewing his brother. The prosecution contended that Mr. Imam had breached the bail conditions by coming into contact with a media person. However, his counsel denied the allegations, arguing that the footage did not establish any direct interaction between Imam and the journalist.

Imam had been granted interim bail from October 4 to October 10 to attend his cousin's wedding functions. The relief was subject to conditions prohibiting him from using social media, interacting with media persons and meeting individuals other than family members, relatives and friends. Taking note of the defence's submission that Mr. Imam had boarded a flight to Delhi and would surrender before jail authorities that evening, the Court declined to cancel his interim bail and disposed of the police application.

articles.title: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled top lawyer on affair with Alice Huang: report
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in ‌response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders’ attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice ​Huang, Jensen Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang misled several of the ‌company’s leaders, including general counsel Tim Teter and Chief Marketing Officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature ​of his relationship with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, with whom he had an affair, ⁠according to two people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by Reuters .
Reuters reviewed several exchanges from October on condition of not quoting verbatim from the messages. The news agency is the first to report on this correspondence.

On Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Huang resigned as ‌Nvidia CEO, a spectacular fall from the chip industry’s heights where he was a pioneer of technology central to the recent boom in artificial intelligence.

He apologised in a statement ‌for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company. His statement did not specifically name Alice ‌Huang, ⁠a former top executive of Nvidia customer Megaspeed International, whom the U.S. was investigating for potentially ⁠spying for China. Jensen Huang and Alice Huang share a last name but are not related.

The New York Times earlier this week reported Mr. Huang also had an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, and Reuters reported on Thursday that Mr. Huang had another intimate relationship with ​a different Nvidia employee.

Mr. Teter did not respond to ‌a request for comment. Mr. Wagonfeld did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A representative for ex-CEO Huang and an Nvidia spokesperson declined to comment. A phone call and email to contact information listed on a business card for Alice Huang went unanswered.

During the autumn of 2025 and in October 2026, in ‌response to press queries that drew some Nvidia leaders’ attention to his relationship with Megaspeed and Alice ​Huang, Mr. Huang at both times described their interactions as appropriate, the people said, speaking on the condition of anonymity. Reuters only reviewed messages from the exchanges in October, not the ⁠ones from 2025.

In two separate messages in October, Mr. Huang told Nvidia leaders that the interactions reflected standard business dealings with customers. In other messages, Mr. Huang affirmed the routine nature of his interactions with Megaspeed.

Nvidia’s Mr. Huang ‌also discussed taking legal action against the New York Times after it published an article in October of last year that drew attention to his meetings in public with Alice Huang, the people said.

That article had prompted Jensen Huang to communicate with some Nvidia leaders in 2025 about their interactions, which he did not describe as an affair, the people said. Ultimately, neither Nvidia nor Mr. Huang filed a lawsuit against the paper. A spokesperson for the New York Times said the paper received no legal demand.

articles.title: Trump administration blames ‘overloaded’ systems for ground stop after FAA lets flights resume
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.
It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.
Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.
The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Asked whether he could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, Mr. Mullin said: “There's nothing completely certain right now. It doesn't appear that way.” He said there are no “footprints” showing an attack and that it appears to be “mechanically driven,” adding that officials were still looking for the cause.

At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

The airports where many of the flights ended up being diverted included Washington Dulles International Airport, Los Angeles International Airport, Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport and Nashville International Airport.
Some 11,000 flights carrying more than 1.5 million passengers had been scheduled to take off from airports in the U.S. after 4 p.m. EST.

Trump administration officials said Friday (November 13, 2026) that new technology being added to the nation's air traffic control system overloaded antiquated systems and caused “intermittent” communications and radar gaps, leading to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years.

It was lifted Friday (November 13, 2026) night after a five-hour stretch when most flights were not allowed to take off from airports in the United States.

Thousands of flights and potentially over a million travellers were affected from coast to coast. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told reporters at the White House that no one was in any danger as more than 3,000 flights were safely landed. But Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy said he could not guarantee it wouldn't happen again.

Mr. Mullin said the FAA was installing “new equipment, new technology” and “it was overwhelming the older system.” There appeared to be no indication of a cyberattack, Mr. Mullin said.

A limited number of domestic flights began departing Friday (November 13, 2026) evening after the ground stop was lifted, but it would likely take days for airlines to fully recover because so many planes and crews were out of position. Officials said they think the system will be back to normal in time to handle the Thanksgiving travel rush.

The nationwide ground stop was the first since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned, and the second since the aftermath of the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

Asked whether he could rule out a cyberattack or rogue artificial intelligence incident, Mr. Mullin said: “There's nothing completely certain right now. At least 827 flights had been diverted. As of 7.05 p.m. EST, 670 flights were sent back to the airport from where they originally took off, while 157 were redirected to a different airport, according to Cirium, an aviation analytics company.

articles.title: SpaceX launches 15th Starship flight with hopes of achieving first round trip
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Starship expected to descend from space after completing 14 orbits around Earth, setting up its debut catch landing for ​Saturday afternoon; the Super Heavy booster was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface

SpaceX launched the 15th flight of its Starship spacecraft from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) on a mission the company hopes will ‌be the first round-trip rocket voyage to orbit and back to the very spot where it left Earth, ​a key test of Elon Musk’s effort to build a fully reusable rocket system.

Plans call for Starship’s uncrewed upper-stage vessel to re-enter ⁠the atmosphere after nearly a day in orbit and return to its launch tower on Saturday (November 14, 2026) for an engine-controlled touchdown assisted by the giant mechanical arms of a pioneering catch-landing mechanism.

SpaceX had intended to use the same return-flight and “chopstick”-arm technology to recover Starship’s lower-stage booster rocket shortly after the two parts of the spacecraft separated within ‌minutes of the launch. But the Super Heavy booster, for reasons not immediately clear, was diverted from its return flight path to a fixed point over the Gulf of Mexico and momentarily hovered in the air before exploding a short distance ‌over the sea surface.
The booster for SpaceX's mega rocket Starship explodes after a catch attempt was aborted during a test flight from Starbase, Texas. | Photo Credit: AP

SpaceX mission controllers hoped to have better luck in steering Starship’s upper stage back to home base at the ‌end ⁠of its flight. The vehicle reached orbit about 27 minutes after launch, SpaceX said.

Bringing the top portion ⁠of the spacecraft intact back to the platform where it was launched would mark a breakthrough in the ambitions of Musk, who founded SpaceX in 2002, to reduce spaceflight costs by developing a fully recyclable rocket system.

The combined vehicle, consisting of the main Starship cargo-and-crew vessel perched atop its Super Heavy booster rocket and standing 40 stories high, roared off its ​launch pad from SpaceX’s South Texas Starbase complex along the ‌Gulf of Mexico near Brownsville.

The flight marked Starship’s 15th test flight since 2023 and the second to carry a batch of operational Starlink satellites to orbit. That makes the mission both a revenue-generating endeavor for SpaceX’s satellite-connectivity business and a high-stakes test for a rocket ship still under development.

Starship 15 began releasing its cargo of 26 satellites about 36 minutes into its flight in a payload-delivery operation expected to take ‌less than an hour to complete, the company said in a livestream presentation of the mission.

Musk’s space and AI business ​views Starship as key to expanding its network of Starlink internet satellites and, in the future, deploying a swarm of orbital AI data-processing centers dubbed Starmind, as the company positions itself to become a high-tech infrastructure provider.

fullParagraphs: Microsoft services are beginning to come back online after a massive global outage left millions of users without access for nearly 18 hours

The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
“We have no indication that the FAA’s nationwide ground stop is related to any Microsoft services,” Microsoft said in an update on social media.
Microsoft says that the company does not have an ETA for a full recovery of Microsoft 365 services yet.
“Still draining queued messages and rebalancing traffic; customers may see improved ⁠sign-in/access,” the company said.

Microsoft, in a post on X, said it was “deeply sorry” for the disruption and was seeing “broad recovery and stability” across its services. It said the outage was a technical issue “not related to cyber or AI / agents”, introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade and surfaced after a recent network change.
It said services were restored gradually, validating stability at each stage, and promised a full post-incident report once its review is complete.
IndiGo said its email support services have been impacted by the Microsoft service disruption. In a post on X, the country’s largest airline said all other support channels remain available.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” the carrier said.

Microsoft 365 has reported improving service availability and email delivery performance across affected infrastructure, adding that there is no indication that the outage was caused by malicious or cyber activity.

articles.title: Piyush Goyal in Egypt: Both sides to discuss increasing cooperation in infra, manufacturing, logistics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.
The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal will begin a two-day visit to Egypt on Sunday (November 15, 2026), focusing on ways to strengthen bilateral trade and investment ties and explore opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, an official statement said.

Egypt's strategic geographical location offers significant opportunities for Indian businesses to strengthen their presence in the country and access markets across Africa, the Middle East and Europe.

The two sides are also expected to discuss measures to facilitate greater participation of businesses in each other's markets, strengthen institutional mechanisms, address trade-related concerns and promote investment partnerships, the commerce ministry said on Saturday (November 14).

"Opportunities for cooperation in the Suez Canal Economic Zone, industrial development, manufacturing, infrastructure, ports and logistics, and regional value chains are also expected to feature in the discussions," it added.

A high-level Indian business delegation comprising over 140 CEOs and senior industry representatives from diverse sectors are accompanying the minister to participate in the India-Egypt Joint Business Council (JBC), and Joint Trade Committee (JTC) meetings.

The seventh session of the JTC will be co-chaired by Mr. Goyal and Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt Mohamed Farid Saleh on Sunday (November 15).

The trade committee meeting will provide an opportunity to review the progress of bilateral trade and investment relations and discuss measures to further diversify and expand the bilateral trade basket.

"Discussions are expected to cover market access issues, non-tariff barriers, trade remedies, agricultural and food products, pharmaceuticals and healthcare, engineering goods, chemicals and petrochemicals, fertilisers, textiles, MSMEs, customs cooperation, services, renewable energy, green hydrogen, transport and logistics," it said.

The JBC Meeting and Business Forum will provide platforms for direct engagement between business leaders and industry stakeholders from both countries to explore opportunities for enhancing bilateral trade and investment, fostering joint ventures, promoting technology partnerships and strengthening industrial collaboration.

During the visit, Mr. Goyal will also hold bilateral meetings with senior Egyptian Ministers to exchange views on further strengthening bilateral economic and commercial relations, particularly in the areas of trade, investment and industrial cooperation.

The postmortem of the bodies of 26 people who died in a collision between a minibus and a container truck in Assam's Kaziranga will be conducted on Saturday (November 14, 2026), Minister Ranoj Pegu said.

articles.title: Kurumba: a language and community fighting for visibility
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kurumbas of Keralam are an Adivasi community with a population of only 2,719 as of 2024, who speak Kurumba, an oral language without a script; with the Census classifying languages with fewer than 10,000 speakers as ‘others’, the future of the language appears bleak

The Kurumbas of Keralam are an Adivasi community who reside in the hilly forest regions of Attappady in Palakkad district. The community has been classified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India. They are one of the five PVTGs in Keralam. As the Census exercise is under way, one of the most significant identifiers of the community is faced with a troubling question.

The community members speak Kurumba, an oral language with no script. This language is widely spoken by the people, even today, and is the primary language of communication among the Kurumba people. However, most outsiders do not use the language and therefore the community members are forced to either learn Malayalam or other languages in order to converse with others.

articles.title: Police fully empowered to curb drugs and substance abuse in the city: Kerala High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The court clarified that the directions issued by the Single Bench would not stand in the way of the police maintaining “requisite vigil and attention” to all activities about drug and substance abuse
The Kerala High Court has observed that the police were fully empowered to enforce every measure to rid the State of drugs and substance abuse.

A division bench comprising Justice Devan Ramachandran and Justice Basant Balaji was considering an appeal filed by the government against a single-bench order setting aside the Kochi city police’s notices imposing restrictions on DJ parties and other events at star hotels, issued to Radisson Blu, a five-star hotel in the city.

The court clarified that the directions issued by the Single Bench would not stand in the way of the police maintaining “requisite vigil and attention” to all activities about drug and substance abuse.
“Prohibition may not always be the best way forward, but rather strict regulation”, the court stated.
Emphasising the role of police in keeping peace in society, the court stated that they should be seen as partners in everyday life, not enemies.

Additional Advocate General Muhammed Shah informed the court that the instructions in the notices issued by the Police were not to restrict the operation of bars until 3 a.m., only against “uncontrolled parties” where drugs and other substances are allegedly used, even openly.

Lawyer Anand Kalyanakrishnan, representing Radisson Blu, informed the court that the hotel was fully responsible for the parties and that they ensure that every customer was carefully screened and scrutinised for carrying drugs or other substances. The matter would be considered for detailed hearing on November 16.

articles.title: Mahadev betting app case: CBI searches in 6 States lead to recovery of digital devices, key documents
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The CBI has conducted searches at 33 locations across six States in connection with its investigation into the Mahadev online betting app case , recovering digital devices, mobile phones and documents indicating the use of mule bank accounts and hawala channels, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
The agency said it conducted searches based on disclosures from Sourabh Chandrakar, one of the platform's principal promoters, following his extradition from Oman.
The searches, carried out over the past few days, targeted premises in Delhi, Mumbai, Nagpur, Amritsar, Bhopal and Raipur, among others, linked to the betting platform's panel operators, they said.
The CBI spokesperson said live betting and gambling panels were found operating at several locations and subsequently dismantled.
The betting app promoter, Chandrakar, was extradited from Oman and arrested by the CBI on November 1.
A special court in Raipur had granted the agency eight days of police custody for his interrogation. He was later sent to judicial custody after the CBI completed its initial questioning.

"His interrogation revealed the details about the working of the platform and its network of panel operators in India," the CBI spokesperson said, adding that he was also confronted with documentary and digital evidence collected during the investigation.

"Investigation conducted so far has revealed that the platform is run from abroad through a Head Office and operates in India through a large network of panel operators," CBI Spokesperson Beena Yadav said in a statement.

She said these operators handle customer IDs, collect betting money in the bank accounts exclusively opened or hired in the names of other persons, and send the profits abroad through hawala channels.
The CBI has registered two FIRs in ₹6000-crore betting scam after the investigations were transferred to the central agency by the Chhattisgarh government.

The CBI has conducted searches at 33 locations across six States in connection with its investigation into the Mahadev online betting app case , recovering digital devices, mobile phones and documents indicating the use of mule bank accounts and hawala channels, officials said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The agency said it conducted searches based on disclosures from Sourabh Chandrakar, one of the platform's principal promoters, following his extradition from Oman.

The searches, carried out over the past few days, targeted premises in Delhi, Mumbai, Nagpur, Amritsar, Bhopal and Raipur, among others, linked to the betting platform's panel operators, they said.

The CBI spokesperson said live betting and gambling panels were found operating at several locations and subsequently dismantled.

The betting app promoter, Chandrakar, was extradited from Oman and arrested by the CBI on November 1.

A special court in Raipur had granted the agency eight days of police custody for his interrogation. He was later sent to judicial custody after the CBI completed its initial questioning.

"His interrogation revealed the details about the working of the platform and its network of panel operators in India," the CBI spokesperson said, adding that he was also confronted with documentary and digital evidence collected during the investigation.

"Investigation conducted so far has revealed that the platform is run from abroad through a Head Office and operates in India through a large network of panel operators," CBI Spokesperson Beena Yadav said in a statement.

She said these operators handle customer IDs, collect betting money in the bank accounts exclusively opened or hired in the names of other persons, and send the profits abroad through hawala channels.

The CBI has registered two FIRs in ₹6000-crore betting scam after the investigations were transferred to the central agency by the Chhattisgarh government.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Trump administration rules out foul play, Transportation Secretary says major communications outage caused by decades old technology

Tens of thousands of fliers were forced to change their plans when the FAA issued a ground stop ‌that lasted four hours and led to the cancellations of more than 6,600 flights, with 8,600 delayed, according to FlightRadar24.
It was just the third nationwide stop issued by ‌the Federal Aviation Administration this century.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the problems not on malicious actors ‌but ⁠on a failure of aging network technology in the radar and communications system used ⁠for air traffic control.

At the Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, where information displays were almost completely filled with flights marked “Delayed” or “Cancelled,” some travellers appeared resigned as they wondered how long the delays would last and how their travel plans would be affected.

NBA, NHL and college teams were left stranded as they tried to reach their destinations. Meanwhile, NFL teams were left to wonder whether the issue would be resolved in time to travel to their games this weekend.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said NCAA teams will be prioritised ahead of football games on Saturday (November 14, 2026).
“I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA, to schedule their flight times and make sure they can move” to make their kickoff, he said.
FedEx, the world’s largest cargo airline, said it was prepared to activate contingency plans to keep any possible disruptions at a minimum.

U.S. airlines move about 61,000 tons (55,340 metric tonnes) of goods — from letters to packages — to and from more than 220 countries daily, according to the industry trade group Airlines for America.
Despite the ground stop, SpaceX launched its Starship rocket from Texas on Friday (November 13, 2026) afternoon in its latest test flight.

articles.title: Trump, Xi and Putin plan unprecedented joint meeting on sidelines of APEC in China: officials
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing

The leaders of the United States, China and Russia plan to meet on November 19, 2026, on the sidelines of next week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China's tech hub of Shenzhen, an unprecedented gathering of the heads of the world's biggest nuclear powers.

While the leaders gathering for joint talks will mark a singular moment, analysts say expectations are low that the talks will lead to major breakthroughs, and they will be heavier in symbolism than substance.

Plans for the three-way summit with Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin were confirmed on Friday (November 13, 2026) by the White House. It comes at a complicated moment in relations between the three countries.

Mr. Trump has warmly embraced Mr. Xi after coming to a truce in their short-lived trade war last year and in spite of differences over the U.S. war with Iran and other tensions between the world's foremost economic powers.

Similarly, Mr. Trump has sought to build his relationship with Mr. Putin, even as the Russian leader has persisted in his nearly five-year-old war with Ukraine and as Moscow has deepened its military, intelligence and diplomatic partnership with Iran.

The U.S. President has insisted that such a meeting would provide an opportunity for the three leaders to discuss the U.S. war with Iran and his goal of reaching a three-way agreement on their nuclear arms stockpiles.

The last nuclear arms pact between Russia and the United States expired in February, removing caps on the two largest atomic arsenals for the first time in more than a half-century. When that treaty — known as New START — expired, Mr. Trump rejected a call by Russia to extend the two-country deal for another year and called for “a new, improved and modernised” deal that includes China.

But Beijing's arsenal of more than 600 warheads, according to Pentagon estimates, is far smaller than inventories held by the U.S. and Russia, each estimated to have more than 5,000 warheads. With U.S. and Russian arsenals dwarfing its stockpile, China has shown little interest in developing a nuclear pact.

By agreeing to host the meeting, Mr. Xi may be calculating that the moment offers him an opportunity to flex China's growing clout and prestige. “I would be shocked if there were a joint statement that came out of this meeting that said anything about denuclearisation,” said Edgard Kagan, a former U.S. ambassador to Malaysia who is now at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies.
For the Kremlin, the planned trilateral meeting is a coveted chance to posture as a superpower on par with Washington and Beijing.

fullParagraphs: Vishwa Hindi Parishad national president Acharya Yarlagadda Lakshmi Prasad on Saturday (November 14, 2026) paid a courtesy call on former President of India Ram Nath Kovind, who is on a visit to Visakhapatnam.

On the occasion, Mr. Lakshmi Prasad presented Hindi and Telugu books authored by him to the former President. Mr Lakshmi Prasad informed Mr. Kovind that he is advancing a mission beneficial to national integration by continuously conducting the “Aadaan – Pradaan” (exchange) programme between the two languages.

He highlighted his efforts in writing books that introduce famous topics and prominent figures from Telugu literature, society, education, and politics to Hindi speakers, while simultaneously writing in Telugu about the unique aspects and personalities of non-Telugu regions at the national level. articles.title: KSSP warns Mission Samudra threatens traditional fishing livelihoods
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Demands curbs on Maritime Board’s sweeping powers; calls for protection of coastal commons and fragile marine ecosystems

The Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad (KSSP) has urged the State government to reconsider Mission Samudra and the proposed Maritime Board Amendment Bill, warning that the initiatives could undermine traditional fishing livelihoods, facilitate corporate control over coastal resources and threaten fragile marine ecosystems.

In a statement, KSSP general secretary V. Manoj Kumar and president C. Ramakrishnan alleged that Mission Samudra, the State’s version of the Union government’s Blue Economy policy, sought to transform Keralam into a port-centric development hub through private participation.

The project envisages the development of 18 minor ports, improved connectivity with major ports such as Vizhinjam, Kochi and Vallarpadam, and the establishment of shipbuilding, repair and breaking facilities. Maritime tourism, a black sand corridor for mineral extraction and the development of Alappuzha as a Blue Economy hub are also proposed.

The parishad expressed concern that the proposed amendments would vest sweeping powers in the Maritime Board, including the creation of a land bank, a Port Area Development Authority and an enforcement wing with police-like powers. Its authority to acquire company shares and lease land for extended periods could turn the board into an instrument for transferring coastal resources to private interests, the signatories warned.

Pointing out that beaches are the principal workplaces of traditional fisherfolk in Keralam’s 222 marine fishing villages, the KSSP said the proposed legislation could undermine their customary rights over these common spaces used for landing catches, marketing fish, storing boats and nets, and drying fish.

It also criticised the project for failing to address the sustainability of Kerala’s annual marine fish catch of around six lakh tonnes or assess the ecological impact of large-scale coastal construction.

The parishad demanded participatory coastal-use mapping, legal protection of traditional fishing rights and safeguards against displacement. It also called for beach restoration, environmentally sustainable port development, protection of traditional fishing routes, and safe housing for coastal communities in the face of climate change.

Further, it demanded that coastal tourism initiatives incorporate fisherfolk through models such as pesca tourism and that Mission Samudra projects receive the consent of local self-government institutions.
The KSSP urged the government to ensure that coastal development does not come at the expense of fishing communities’ livelihoods, customary rights and environmental security.
