🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 14 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 3 Min Read

📰 KSSP warns Mission Samudra threatens traditional fishing livelihoods

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Demands curbs on Maritime Board’s sweeping powers; calls for protection of coastal commons and fragile marine ecosystems

The Kerala Sasthra Sahithya Parishad (KSSP) has urged the State government to reconsider Mission Samudra and the proposed Maritime Board Amendment Bill, warning that the initiatives could undermine traditional fishing livelihoods, facilitate corporate control over coastal resources and threaten fragile marine ecosystems.

In a statement, KSSP general secretary V. Manoj Kumar and president C. Ramakrishnan alleged that Mission Samudra, the State’s version of the Union government’s Blue Economy policy, sought to transform Keralam into a port-centric development hub through private participation.

The project envisages the development of 18 minor ports, improved connectivity with major ports such as Vizhinjam, Kochi and Vallarpadam, and the establishment of shipbuilding, repair and breaking facilities. Maritime tourism, a black sand corridor for mineral extraction and the development of Alappuzha as a Blue Economy hub are also proposed.

The parishad expressed concern that the proposed amendments would vest sweeping powers in the Maritime Board, including the creation of a land bank, a Port Area Development Authority and an enforcement wing with police-like powers. Its authority to acquire company shares and lease land for extended periods could turn the board into an instrument for transferring coastal resources to private interests, the signatories warned.

Pointing out that beaches are the principal workplaces of traditional fisherfolk in Keralam’s 222 marine fishing villages, the KSSP said the proposed legislation could undermine their customary rights over these common spaces used for landing catches, marketing fish, storing boats and nets, and drying fish.

It also criticised the project for failing to address the sustainability of Kerala’s annual marine fish catch of around six lakh tonnes or assess the ecological impact of large-scale coastal construction.

The parishad demanded participatory coastal-use mapping, legal protection of traditional fishing rights and safeguards against displacement. It also called for beach restoration, environmentally sustainable port development, protection of traditional fishing routes, and safe housing for coastal communities in the face of climate change.

Further, it demanded that coastal tourism initiatives incorporate fisherfolk through models such as pesca tourism and that Mission Samudra projects receive the consent of local self-government institutions.

The KSSP urged the government to ensure that coastal development does not come at the expense of fishing communities’ livelihoods, customary rights and environmental security.

articles.title: Year-long Constitution awareness campaign to begin on November 26
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Dalit Sangharsha Samithigala Aikya Horata Chalana Samithi, Bengaluru, in association with the Samvidhana Janandolana Samithi-Karnataka, will launch a year-long awareness campaign titled ‘Voice of Constitution, Voice of Public’ on November 26, as part of the State government’s Constitution Day celebrations.

Sharing details of the programme at a press conference here on Saturday, Samithi State Coordinator Indudhara Honnapur said the year-long Constitution awareness campaign would be formally launched at the KSOU Convocation Hall at 3 p.m. on November 26. The launch programme would follow the State government’s event to mark Constitution Day.

“There will be a government programme in the morning. We support it and will participate in it,” Mr. Honnapur said, adding that the Samithi had initially planned a two-day programme, but had subsequently decided to restrict it to one day.

Former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah will inaugurate the awareness campaign, while former Minister H.C. Mahadevappa will preside over the programme. Former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y. Quraishi will deliver a talk on the Constitution and Democratic Values. Writer Baragur Ramachandrappa will deliver the inaugural address.

The main focus of the year-long awareness campaign is to strengthen the AHINDA (an acronym for backward classes, minorities and Dalits). The campaign will include study camps, debates, discussions and seminars across all 31 districts in the State.

When asked why the Samithi was focusing on AHINDA despite a Dalit leader not being considered for the Chief Minister’s post when former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah stepped down, its members said there were no differences of opinion within the organisation on the issue. They maintained that the Samithi was not a political platform and that the welfare of the community, particularly the AHINDA sections, remained its primary objective.

Mr. Honnapur demanded that the proposed delimitation exercise be dropped, arguing that it would be a disadvantage for southern States because of their relatively lower populations compared to northern States.

The Samithi accused the State government of allegedly diverting funds allocated under the Scheduled Caste Sub-Plan (SCSP) and Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP) for implementing guarantee schemes. Mr. Honnapur alleged that funds earmarked for the welfare of Dalits were being diverted to other schemes and said that Dalit organisations would launch a campaign against the move.
The Samithi also urged the government to implement a single-window system for SCSP and TSP funds.

articles.title: KPSC ‘recruitment scam’: ED attaches properties worth ₹1.22 crore belonging to former chairman, member and IAS officer
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The three officials allegedly abused their official positions to collect illegal gratification from candidates in exchange for assured selection through question paper leaks, supply of candidate-specific answer keys and manipulation of confidential marks during the preparation of the 1:3 eligibility list

The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has provisionally attached movable and immovable properties worth ₹1.22 crore belonging to three former senior functionaries of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC ) in connection with the veterinary officer recruitment scam.

Those whose properties have been attached include former KPSC chairman Shivashankarappa Sahukar , commission member Geetha B.V. Shivamurthy and IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar , who was then Controller of Examinations.
The attachment order was issued on Friday (November 13) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002.

According to the ED investigation, the three officials allegedly abused their official positions in conspiracy with Basavaraj Kannale, a middleman, and others in order to collect illegal gratification from candidates in exchange for assured selection through question paper leaks, supply of candidate-specific answer keys and manipulation of confidential marks during preparation of the 1:3 eligibility list.

The investigation revealed that Mr. Gangwar allegedly leaked question papers, with the correct answers marked, to his close associate, Mr. Kannale, on January 7, 2026, the ED said. Mr. Kannale allegedly circulated the papers among 10 candidates at villas on the outskirts of Bengaluru on January 8, a day before the examination.

He reportedly demanded bribes ranging from ₹20 lakh to ₹40 lakh from candidates. A portion of the money was allegedly collected in advance, while the remaining amounts were secured through blank signed cheques and promissory notes.

The ED claimed that the OMR answer sheets of these candidates matched the initial answer key published by the KPSC, including answers that were subsequently declared incorrect in the revised answer key.

In another instance, at the alleged insistence of Mr. Sahukar, Mr. Gangwar allegedly used confidential seating arrangements and jumbled charts, which were under his custody, to prepare correct answers to 80 questions for six candidates.

The registration numbers of these candidates were allegedly provided by Ms. Geetha on January 8, and the answers were handed over to her. In return, the then chairman allegedly assured Mr. Gangwar of favourable interview marks in the KAS examination for a candidate of his choice.

The ED also seized a notebook from Mr. Sahukar’s residence containing centre-wise registration numbers of candidates, allegedly written in his handwriting. Mr. Sahukar allegedly collected ₹10 lakh in cash from one candidate against a deal of ₹20 lakh, while Ms. Geetha allegedly collected ₹20 lakh from another candidate against a deal of ₹40 lakh.

articles.title: Mass awareness rally held in Mysuru against drug abuse
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Campaign under NALSA initiative focuses on protecting students and youth from substance abuse

Emphasising the need to protect young people from substance abuse, First Additional District and Sessions Judge Sandhya Rao P. called upon the youth to stay away from addictive substances and adopt a healthy lifestyle.
She was speaking after inaugurating an awareness rally against drug abuse organised under the NALSA’s DAWN (Drug Awareness and Wellness Navigation) initiative in Mysuru.

The programme was jointly organised by the District Legal Services Authority, Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, Department of Justice, Mysuru Bar Association, Police Department and JSS Law College (Autonomous), along with other departments and organisations.

Ms. Rao said the primary objective of the campaign was to protect students and the younger generation from the harmful effects of narcotic substances. The youth were the future of the country and should not fall prey to addiction under any circumstances, she said.
The campaign sought to create awareness, particularly among children in the 12-18 age group and students, about the dangers of drug abuse.

The rally began at JSS Law College and passed through prominent junctions before culminating near the Old Court Complex, where floral tributes were paid to the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. Students raised slogans against drug abuse and carried placards highlighting its harmful consequences.

Senior Civil Judge and Member-Secretary of the District Legal Services Authority Nagaraj Siddappa Ankasadoddi, Additional Superintendent of Police Mallik C., Central Prison Chief Superintendent Sheshumurthy V., Deputy Director of the Department of Women and Child Development R. Nagaraj, Bar Association president S. Lokesh, JSS Law College Chief Executive K.S. Suresh and principal N. Vanishree were present.
Officials from various departments, doctors, panel advocates, college students and practitioners of the Heartfulness Institute also participated.

articles.title: Myanmar airstrike on displaced persons camp kills 12, say witnesses
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions

A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp housing people displaced by the civil war killed 12 people in the westernmost state of Rakhine, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Chit Su Wai, a 27-year-old shopkeeper, sobbed as she described how her daughter, aunt and mother were killed on Friday evening (November 13, 2026) in Byar La IDP camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of state capital Sittwe.

"All I saw was their bodies scattered in pain. I could not find words to describe it. And we were lost with crying," she said. "It has broken our family. There were no others except my family. We did not hear the sound of the fighter jet — it just came and dropped the bombs."
Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says

Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions that have long held sway in the nation's fringes.

The western coastal state of Rakhine is among the regions worst hit by the war. Controlled almost entirely by the ethnic minority Arakan Army (AA), it has been blockaded by the military and pummelled with regular airstrikes. It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment on the latest attack.

Chit Su Wai said 12 people died in Friday's attack, a toll confirmed by Khine Hein Htet, chairman of the Phyusin Yin Khwin Foundation, a rescue and emergency service. Khine Hein Htet said a five-year-old was among the dead, while 18 were also injured in the camp, where many residents had been living for four years.

"They believed the camp was safe, and they sheltered there together. When we arrived at the scene, most of the victims had died in one place," the 24-year-old said. He said it was not a combat area, adding: "We never thought this camp would be targeted."

The village was a mess of collapsed bamboo houses on Saturday, the wreckage of an upturned vehicle mixed among the debris of household goods and clothes. Locals had already removed the bodies, wrapping them in yellow and red plastic and burying them in makeshift graves.

Aung Kyaw Min, a 45-year-old tuktuk driver, described how he rushed to the village where his brother and sister lived after hearing of the attack. "My sister's body was already headless while my brother was lying dead," he said, crying.

Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions

A Myanmar military airstrike on a camp housing people displaced by the civil war killed 12 people in the westernmost state of Rakhine, witnesses and a rescue worker said on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

Chit Su Wai, a 27-year-old shopkeeper, sobbed as she described how her daughter, aunt and mother were killed on Friday evening (November 13, 2026) in Byar La IDP camp in Ponnagyun township, northeast of state capital Sittwe.

"All I saw was their bodies scattered in pain. I could not find words to describe it. And we were lost with crying," she said. "It has broken our family. There were no others except my family. We did not hear the sound of the fighter jet — it just came and dropped the bombs."

Myanmar army seizes key resistance headquarters and 10 bases held by opposition, state media says

Myanmar has been consumed by civil war since the military staged a coup five years ago, provoking armed resistance from democracy activists and ethnic minority factions that have long held sway in the nation's fringes.

The western coastal state of Rakhine is among the regions worst hit by the war. Controlled almost entirely by the ethnic minority Arakan Army (AA), it has been blockaded by the military and pummelled with regular airstrikes. It was not possible to contact the Myanmar military for comment on the latest attack.

Chit Su Wai said 12 people died in Friday's attack, a toll confirmed by Khine Hein Htet, chairman of the Phyusin Yin Khwin Foundation, a rescue and emergency service. Khine Hein Htet said a five-year-old was among the dead, while 18 were also injured in the camp, where many residents had been living for four years.

"They believed the camp was safe, and they sheltered there together. When we arrived at the scene, most of the victims had died in one place," the 24-year-old said. He said it was not a combat area, adding: "We never thought this camp would be targeted."

The village was a mess of collapsed bamboo houses on Saturday, the wreckage of an upturned vehicle mixed among the debris of household goods and clothes. Locals had already removed the bodies, wrapping them in yellow and red plastic and burying them in makeshift graves.

Aung Kyaw Min, a 45-year-old tuktuk driver, described how he rushed to the village where his brother and sister lived after hearing of the attack. "My sister's body was already headless while my brother was lying dead," he said, crying.

articles.title: Pakistani Minister to visit India for the first time in three years, as SCO meets
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The last such high-level visit to India was by then Foreign Minister Bilawal ‌Bhutto Zardari, who ​travelled to Goa in ⁠May 2023 for a meeting of SCO Foreign Ministers

Pakistan’s Climate Minister Musadik Masood Malik will represent the country at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilizational Dialogue to be held in New Delhi from November 20-22, 2026, the country’s Foreign Ministry said in a statement. This marks the first visit by a Pakistani minister to India in more than three years.
“The Government of Pakistan remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual,” reads the statement.
The last such high-level visit to India was by then Foreign Minister Bilawal ‌Bhutto Zardari, who ​travelled to Goa in ⁠May 2023 for a meeting of SCO Foreign Ministers.
The ‌SCO is a political and security union of countries spanning much of Eurasia, including China and Russia. The regional bloc has ‌10 current members, according to ​its website.

articles.title: U.S. proposes Ukraine cede territory in exchange for joining NATO: Zelensky
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia had rejected a ceasefire on energy targets at talks in Abu Dhabi, as Moscow was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign

Mr. Zelensky said Russia was “betting everything” on this winter’s campaign in its war with Ukraine, while warning that the Kremlin’s demands to redraw Europe’s security architecture were “dangerous” and could lead to more wars.

Mr. Zelensky spoke to the media on Friday (November 13, 2026), after visits to Denmark and Ireland, where he met European leaders following two days of U.S.-brokered Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi. The talks ended with no breakthrough in Europe’s worst war since the Second World War, but all sides agreed that European officials should be included in future negotiations.
U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff attended the Abu Dhabi talks, and then met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Mr. Zelensky separately.
Moscow turned down a proposal for a ceasefire in attacks on energy targets at the Abu Dhabi talks, Mr. Zelensky said. “On the proposal for an energy ceasefire: the Russians don’t want it,” he said.

He said Mr. Putin’s proposal for a “humanitarian mission” to Kostiantynivka was a ploy to get Kyiv to withdraw from the embattled city and open the road to more settlements in the Donetsk region. “Putin simply wants us to leave Kostiantynivka so that they can move in and occupy the entire city that way,” he said. Russia said this year that it had seized the town, but Ukraine has said fighting is continuing.

Moscow’s troops have inched westwards since launching the invasion in February 2022, but have been unable to seize the whole of the Donetsk region. Mr. Zelensky said the EU and NATO are Europe’s “only real security”, and that Moscow’s bid to review the continent’s security was “dangerous because... it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations.”

articles.title: Indian Railways to connect Nepal’s Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya through weekly train service
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations
Indian Railways is going to operate a new weekly train service between Janakpur Dham in Nepal and Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh.

The Ministry of Railways stated in a statement on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that the initiative is to link two places which are associated with “the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace Lord Ram.”
The route will cover approximately 604 kilometres, connecting Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt., passing through several towns and cities in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
The train will have stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur, and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.
Railways Ministry said that the service will operate once a week, with its originating days being Saturday from Janakpur Dham and Monday from Ayodhya Cantt.

Citing the role of railway connectivity on bilateral cooperation, the Ministry said in a statement, “India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer.”
India and Nepal have held discussions on cross-border railway links, including passenger train services on the Janakpur-Ayodhya section, and bilateral cooperation in the sector in June this year.

U.S. authorities believe the alleged plot to kill Khalistani activist, Gurpatwant Singh Pannun, who is wanted on terror charges in India, was ordered by the previous chief of the Indian Research and Analysis Wing (R&AW), and had official sanction from senior intelligence officials with “with ties to [Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s inner circle”, the Washington Post, a U.S.-national daily, reported .

The report in the Washington Post newspaper identified, for the first time, an R&AW officer whose name had been withheld in the case papers made available by the Justice Department in New York in November 2023. In a separate press release, the Post said, on the basis of interviews with “more than three dozen current and former senior officials in the United States, India, Canada, Britain, Germany and Australia”, that other R&AW officers have faced “arrest, expulsion and reprimand” in recent months, indicating that there was more international coordination about what it called “escalating campaign of aggression” against Indian diaspora members by India’s intelligence operatives.

The Ministry of External Affairs declined to comment on the latest story in the Washington Post report on Monday. Last week, in response to a question on the allegations, the MEA spokesperson said that a “high-level committee is looking into information that was shared by the American side with us, because [it] also equally impacts our national security. In recent weeks, the government has also blocked the broadcast of documentaries by Canadian and Australian public broadcasters CBC and ABC that focussed on the allegations against Indian agencies for targeting Khalistani activists abroad.

“In reports that have been closely held within the American government, U.S. intelligence officials have assessed that the operation targeting Pannun was approved by the RAW chief at the time, Samant Goel,” said the report. “U.S. spy agencies have more tentatively assessed that Mr. Modi’s National Security Adviser, Ajit Doval, was probably aware of RAW’s plans to kill Sikh activists,” it added.

According to the story, the R&AW official identified as Vikash Yadav had directed Indian businessman Nikhil Gupta, now in custody in the Czech Republic pending extradition to the U.S. to stand trial in the case, to hire a hitman to kill GS Pannun outside his New York residence. Mr. Yadav, believed to be a Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) official on deputation to the R&AW, has subsequently been repatriated to the paramilitary forces, other U.S. media have reported.

While the MEA Ministry of External Affairs has maintained that such killings are not Indian policy, and has denied Canadian allegations of a similar hit on Khalistani activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar in Canada, the government has agreed to an enquiry on the U.S. allegations.
The Washington Post story also dwells at length on differences between the U.S. White House administration and the Justice Department that oversaw the FBI-DEA investigation in the case.

The evidence cited had included an undercover American agent who was hired for the Pannun killing by Mr. Gupta, under direct orders from Mr. Yadav, surveillance of messages purportedly exchanged between them, as well as a photograph allegedly showing three Indian intelligence officials who gave the green signal for the plot during a video-call.

However, the report stated while the Justice Department pushed for an indictment against both Mr. Gupta and Mr. Yadav, Biden administration officials prevailed in ensuring the indictment is against only Mr. Gupta at present, ostensibly so as not to “rupture” ties with India.

The matter was thrashed out a series of meetings which included U.S. Deputy NSA Jon Finer, U.S. Deputy Attorney General Lisa Monaco and Deputy CIA Director David Cohen, the report said. It also stated Mr. President Biden had discussed the issue with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting in September 2023, calling for accountability for the case.

articles.title: Age of AI: behind Tarluvada’s blue wall in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: As construction for hyperscale Google AI data centres go full throttle in Visakhapatnam, farmers say promised land and jobs have not arrived

The muddy, unpaved road into Tarluvada runs along a wall of tall blue corrugated iron sheets. Once, it was just farms and forests. What is being built behind the wall is hidden from view. Just beyond, on the hill locals call Chukka Konda, a broad swathe of the slope has been stripped back to red earth and cut into terraces, stark against the green around it.

Last year, when government officials came to the small village in Anandapuram mandal on the outskirts of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, they had made big promises: plentiful jobs and opportunities once Google, the American tech corporation, built its hyperscale 1 GW AI data centre there. Today, the village is uneasy. Many farmers refuse to talk. Leaders of Left parties say they are not allowed to meet the locals to understand their problems, and those who speak to them are being targeted and harassed by the police.

articles.title: ‘Abki baar, AQI 400-paar’: Congress takes a swipe at Modi over Delhi pollution
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Jairam Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult

The Congress on Saturday (November 14, 2026) took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over his 2024 Lok Sabha election slogan, “Abki baar, 400-paar”, saying it had come true in the national capital, with Delhi’s air quality index (AQI) crossing the 400-mark.
In a post in Hindi on X, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said, “Abki baar, AQI 400-paar. The ‘pravachanmantri’s’ (preaching minister) slogan is coming true when it comes to AQI!”

Referring to reports of worsening air quality in Delhi, Mr. Ramesh said the city had become the most polluted in the world, with toxic air making breathing difficult. Children and the elderly were bearing the brunt of the pollution, while the number of patients in hospitals was rising, he said.
“Slogans were tossed into the air; now the air itself has turned to poison,” he said.
Mr. Modi had used the “Abki baar, 400-paar” slogan during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign, seeking a mandate of more than 400 seats for the National Democratic Alliance.

Several air quality monitoring stations in Delhi have recorded AQI levels in the ‘severe’ category (400-500) over the past few days. The city’s average AQI had also crossed the 400-mark on Friday (November 13, 2026).

articles.title: Avian influenza confirmed in Tamil Nadu’s Cuddalore; over 1,500 chickens culled
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13
Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (H5N1) has been confirmed in chicken samples collected from a poultry farm at Kattiyankuppam village in Kurinjipadi taluk of Cuddalore district.

“The National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD), Bhopal, had confirmed the H5N1 avian influenza virus in samples collected from a poultry carcass on November 5, 2026,” District Collector Sibi Adhithya Senthil Kumar told The Hindu .

The confirmation has triggered a full-scale containment operation, with the Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services Department culling all birds in the affected farm and within a one-kilometre radius of the epicentre.

According to Mr. Senthil Kumar: “As many as 35,647 bird deaths were recorded in the affected belt till November 13, since the first case of sudden mortality was reported from a farm at Thamanampatti village in Thiyagavalli Panchayat on October 30.”
He added, “Veterinary teams that visited the farm on the day of the first report collected samples and sent them to the Poultry Disease Diagnostic Laboratory (PDDL) in Namakkal.”

As deaths mounted in neighbouring farms, further samples were routed to Poultry Disease Diagnosis and Surveillance Laboratory (PDDL) Erode and the Central University Laboratory (CUL) at Madhavaram in Chennai.
On November 5, a carcass sample was despatched to NIHSAD Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 on November 13, he said.
Following the standard operating procedure under the National Action Plan, the district was divided into compartments to restrict the spread of the disease.

“Initially, we sent only one sample. But a total of 15 farms are affected, of which all the birds in 10 farms have already been wiped out. So only five farms remain, and we are going to cull all [the birds] anyway. As many as nine Rapid Response Teams have been deployed for this purpose,” the Collector said.

So far, 1,550 birds have been humanely culled, and the department is working to cull 100% of the birds in the epicentre farm and within the 1-km radius, in accordance with the Government of India guidelines, 2021.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

Editorial Context: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

🎯 Exam Relevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions

Any regulation of crackers needs strict enforcement at all levels

The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: Without peace, Israel risks descending into chaos

Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.
Editorial Context: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance 📅 13 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
🔮 Futuristic Word Radar: Paragraph ke kisi bhi English word par Double-Click karein — turant uska Hinglish Meaning + Picture screen par dekhein!

Several industry bodies have been meeting top officials of the Finance Ministry as part of the annual pre-Budget consultation process

Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Ultra Premium Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: India must improve ties with Bangladesh, and protect Hasina

Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

Editorial Context: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties. This editorial examines the institutional, constitutional, and pragmatic dimensions shaping public policy and governance in India.

fullParagraphs: West Bengal has witnessed a sudden, rapid spike in attacks on Christian home fellowships and churches since the summer of 2026, when the BJP government came to power in the State. Senjuti Sengupta and Shiv Sahay Singh report on the fear of the community that is less than 1% of the population in West Bengal

A 65-year-old woman, Purnima (name changed to protect privacy), had eagerly waited for October 31, 2026, when a new church was to be inaugurated in front of her house. Her family had donated a significant amount of land and the freshly painted white building of William Cary Memorial Church was ready to welcome devotees at Narayantala village in Basanti block of West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district. Now, she shudders when she thinks about what happened on that Saturday afternoon to the church.

“The gate of the church was opened for the first and the last time on October 31. During the inaugural function, a group entered the premises and attacked the priests and others who were participating in the ceremony,” Purnima says, recalling the attack that left her and several others injured. She says she was hit with a stick and had to be hospitalised for a day. After the attack, the church has been closed, but Purnima says she often goes to its door to peek at the picture of Jesus Christ through a broken window.

articles.title: Sukhbir Badal likely to meet Amit Shah on November 13, SAD-BJP alliance may be announced this month
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: SAD sources said that Mr. Badal is likely to leave for New Delhi after his rally at Raikot to meet Mr. Shah, with talks on seat sharing and finalising the alliance on the agenda

After months of speculation over a possible re-alliance between the old partners Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly election, a likely meeting between SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal and Union Home Minister Amit Shah on November 13 is being viewed as a move toward sealing the alliance.

SAD sources said that Mr. Badal is expected to leave for New Delhi in the second half of the day, after his rally at Raikot, to meet Mr. Shah. It is expected that the talks surrounding the seat sharing and finalisation of the alliance for the Punjab election would be on the agenda. Even as leaders from both parties remained tight-lipped about the deliberations, the sources indicated that the announcement about the alliance could be made within November.

In August this year, Mr. Badal had met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi, where the possibility of renewing the alliance was discussed. A SAD source had confirmed that, with discussions underway, an alliance could materialise.

The SAD and the BJP were alliance partners since the late 1990s, however, amid the controversy over the Centre’s agriculture sector laws, which were later repealed, the SAD — one of the BJP’s oldest alliance partners — decided to break away from the NDA coalition in 2020.

articles.title: West Bengal government to appoint coordinators if stay on civic polls not lifted, says CM Adhikari
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted

The West Bengal government will appoint coordinators in the wards of Kolkata Municipal Corporation and Howrah Municipal Corporation if the stay on civic polls is not lifted by the Supreme Court, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

The Calcutta High Court on October 6 restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming KMC elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

Addressing a gathering in Howrah District, Mr. Adhikari accused Opposition parties of obstructing the electoral process, and alleged that residents had been deprived of elected civic representation and proper municipal services for years.

“Those who are likely to lose their security deposits in the elections are the ones obstructing the process,” the Chief Minister said. He said that similar to proposal at KMC, coordinators will be appointed for each ward in Howrah Municipal Corporation (HMC) if elections are not held in time. According to sources, BJP leaders are likely to be appointed as coordinators across KMC and HMC.

Mr. Adhikari said that his government would approach the Supreme Court with a Special Leave Petition (SLP) seeking that the stay on holding civic polls be lifted. According to the Chief Minister, officials have limitations and cannot provide civic facilities for a long time.

Elections to the HMC have not been held since 2013, and for almost a decade officials have been providing services to the people of the civic body. The Trinamool Congress run board at Kolkata Municipal Corporation was dissolved weeks after the Bharatiya Janata Party government came to power. Mayor of KMC Firhad Hakim and other councillors resigned and the State government appointed an administrator to run the affairs of the largest civic body in the State.

The Calcutta High Court on Friday (October 6, 2026) restrained the West Bengal State Election Commission from issuing any notification for the upcoming Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) elections based on newly redrawn wards until a pending petition challenging the delimitation exercise is decided.

The West Bengal government had passed a legislation in the State Assembly on August 12, redrawing the wards of the KMC and HMC increasing the number of wards from 144 to 209 and 50 to 68 respectively. The Opposition parties have alleged the State government and its agencies have resorted to gerrymandering while undertaking delimitation of wards in order to secure partisan advantage to the ruling political party in West Bengal on the premise of previous electoral results.

The BJP government in West Bengal was keen on holding elections to KMC and HMC. In fact, the BJP leadership had started the process of selecting candidates. Mr. Adhikari has on several occasions, expressed their preference to hold civic body elections in Kolkata and Howrah by the end of November or early December this year.

articles.title: TNPDCL seeks nod to procure 3,000 MW
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum
The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation Limited (TNPDCL) has increased the quantum of its proposed power procurement from 1,500 megawatt (MW) to 3,000 MW through a medium-term tender agreement.
The TNPDCL, which submitted the proposal to procure 1,500 MW to the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission (TNERC) in February this year, has now doubled the quantum.

A senior TNPDCL official said amid a power demand of about 19,000 MW and an extended summer, it has been proposed to buy 3,000 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power for five years, under the Finance, Operate and Own guidelines.

TNERC will take up the application for medium-term power purchase, along with requests for deviation from the guidelines and permission to float a short-term tender to procure RTC and peak-hour power for the period from February to July next year.

TNPDCL submitted in its application that the annual power demand had increased to 22,000 MW from an average of 18,000 MW due to various factors, including changes in weather pattern, increasing migrant population, and a surge in electric vehicle sales, with the State set to face an energy shortage of 7,000 MW by 2029-30.
The senior official said the long-term power purchase agreements signed for a quantum of 2,830 MW would expire by 2028-29, prompting new procurement plans.
The estimated cost of the medium-term procurement is around ₹5.50 per kilo watt per hour, with the annual expenditure pegged at ₹6,150 crore.
When the State faced a power shortage this October, TNPDCL had to purchase power at a cost of ₹30 per unit to bridge the peak-hour gap.

articles.title: Yemen’s Houthis say they targeted Saudi East-West pipeline, port city of Yanbu
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The East-West pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to Saudi Arabia, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula
Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday (November 12, 2026) that their forces targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in the port city of Yanbu on the Red Sea.

The pipeline, which ends at Yanbu, has become increasingly important to the world's largest crude exporter, allowing it to get its oil to market after Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz on the other side of the Arabian Peninsula at the outset of the West Asia war.

Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said in a post on X that one operation "targeted Pumping Station No. 7 on the East-West Pipeline using a drone", while a second "targeted the Yanbu oil facility using a ballistic missile".
He claimed both attacks — as well as two others launched at a Saudi airport and an airbase not far from the Yemeni border — had been successful.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted the East-West pipeline, and on Monday (November 9, 2026) Saudi Arabia said an attack on the conduit had sparked a fire but had not affected operations.
Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage.
A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack".

Saree also said the Houthis had attacked state-run oil company Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with a drone, though there were no immediate reports of damage.

A skyscraper belonging to the oil giant was hit on Sunday (November 8, 2026) by what authorities described as falling shrapnel from an "attempted attack".

articles.title: Widespread outage hits Microsoft apps
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Microsoft said that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors”; it determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks

A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday (November 12, 2026), with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.

Nearly 1,30,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn’t send and receive emails, or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.
Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft’s workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.
Microsoft said that it was investigating disruptions, notably related to its email and Teams applications.

In updates posted on social media, Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft said it was aware of users “experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas.”

Microsoft later explained that a portion of its infrastructure was “experiencing elevated load” — which it said was “likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” The company determined a number of servers were “unexpectedly unavailable” due to a problem that caused them to fail during automated checks.
Microsoft did not immediately provide more information around what might be causing that failure, but added that it was testing a fix.
“We’re aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact,” the Microsoft 365 Status account wrote on X.
Earlier in the day, the company said it had “successfully restored” problems related to Microsoft Teams in North America, although some users continued to report connectivity issues.

articles.title: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The U.K.-India climate partnership shows what delivery can look like in practice. Both our countries recognise that the shift to cleaner growth is not separate from the pursuit of prosperity

Next week, Mumbai will become the stage for one of the world’s boldest climate ideas. The largest ever Earthshot Prize edition will bring together innovators, investors, businesses, policymakers and young people to turn environmental solutions into impact at scale. Five winners will each receive £1 million to accelerate their work.

It all began with a simple but powerful idea: that human ingenuity, innovation and optimism can help repair our planet. Founded by His Royal Highness The Prince of Wales, The Earthshot Prize seeks solutions capable of delivering transformative environmental impact. Since the Prize was launched in 2020, India has produced more Earthshot finalists and winners than any other country (nine finalists including four winners). This year two of the 15 finalists are based in India. As the Prize arrives in Mumbai, India’s growing influence in clean growth and climate innovation will be on full display.

Science, Space & Environment Report: India and U.K. are turning climate ambition into action. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Eight-year-old undergoes endoscopic treatment for rare swallowing disorder
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The child, diagnosed with Type II achalasia, underwent a minimally invasive procedure at Rela Hospital in Chennai

An eight-year-old boy diagnosed with Type II achalasia – a rare disorder that affects the ability to swallow food and liquids – has undergone a Perora-l Endoscopic Myotomy (POEM) procedure at Rela Hospital.

Achalasia affects the nerves controlling the muscles of the oesophagus, causing the lower oesophageal sphincter – a muscular valve connecting the food pipe to the stomach – to remain abnormally tight. This prevents food and liquids from passing normally into the stomach. The condition is estimated to affect 0.1 to 0.18 children per 100,000 annually.

The child had progressively worsening difficulty swallowing both solids and liquids. Following the procedure, he was able to resume consuming clear liquids and subsequently, a soft diet, within 24 hours.

POEM involves passing an endoscope through the mouth and creating a small tunnel within the oesophageal wall to reach and divide the muscle fibres causing the obstruction. Unlike conventional surgery, the procedure does not require external incisions or stitches.

S.N.K. Chenduran, senior consultant and endoscopic surgeon, Department of Medical Gastroenterology, performed the procedure, which took about 50 minutes. He said performing POEM in children required particular precision because of the smaller dimensions of the oesophagus and the delicate tissues.

Dinesh Jothimani, director, Hepatology and Medical Gastroenterology, said persistent swallowing difficulties, regurgitation, vomiting, and unexplained weight loss in children warranted medical evaluation.

Her family had donated a significant amount of land and the freshly painted white building of William Cary Memorial Church was ready to welcome devotees at Narayantala village in Basanti block of West Bengal’s South 24 Parganas district. Now, she shudders when she thinks about what happened on that Saturday afternoon to the church.

During the inaugural function, a group entered the premises and attacked the priests and others who were participating in the ceremony,” Purnima says, recalling the attack that left her and several others injured. She says she was hit with a stick and had to be hospitalised for a day. After the attack, the church has been closed, but Purnima says she often goes to its door to peek at the picture of Jesus Christ through a broken window.

articles.title: Sriperumbudur toll plaza gets MLFF

fullParagraphs: The scanners will read FASTag cards and number plates, and the system will automatically collect the amount due at the toll

Motorists using the Sriperumbudur toll plaza on the Chennai-Bengaluru National Highway from Wednesday midnight will be able to drive freely without stopping for boom barriers. . This is the second plaza in the State to get multi-lane free flow tolling, where gantries with scanners have been installed. The scanners will read FASTag cards and number plates, and the system will automatically collect the amount due at the toll. The facility will allow motorists to drive through, without having to wait at the plaza, which caters to over 1.25 lakh vehicles on a daily basis.

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir: ‘More the bhakts comment, better it would do,’ says Rahul Gandhi on BJP’s criticisms
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Responding to a question during an ‘Ask Me’ session on Instagram, Rahul Gandhi said, “It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can’t resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it”

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Friday took a swipe at the BJP leaders over their criticism of former AICC chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir, saying the more the "Bhakts" comment on the book, the better it would do.
He also claimed that a lot of the BJP leaders secretly like his mother and think she is fantastic "but unfortunately can't say it".

Responding to a question during an 'Ask Me' session on Instagram as to why the BJP is talking so much about Sonia Gandhi's just-released book "Belonging: A Journey Of Love", Gandhi said, "It is a great book, they are all reading it. They can't resist reading it and then they have got to comment on it."

articles.title: Forming fact-finding panel by agitating students unauthorised, aimed at fomenting tension: SRFTI
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, since September 27, has been investigated by a special investigation team constituted by the West Bengal government

SRFTI authorities said an independent fact-finding exercise initiated by a group of protesting students into the campus crisis was "unauthorised", claiming that such an attempt was aimed at "distorting the factual record, fomenting tension and undermining the ongoing SIT probe".

The Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, under the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said several incidents, including alleged attacks on students, since September 27 have been investigated by a special investigation team constituted by the West Bengal government, and questioned the legitimacy of a "parallel probe by an external organisation".
SRFTI Registrar Deepak Kumar said on Thursday (November 13, 2026) night that the institute had also constituted its own fact-finding committee to inquire into alleged violence on the campus.

"The matter is already under investigation by an SIT constituted by the West Bengal government. The institute has also constituted its own fact-finding committee to examine the incidents," Mr. Kumar said.
He alleged that the "parallel exercise is aimed at creating competing narratives, distorting the factual record and undermining the ongoing investigation".
Mr. Kumar alluded to a statement by agitating students to form a fact-finding panel on their part to probe the incidents, including alleged violence on the campus, since September 27.

"Such an attempt appears aimed at fomenting tension and keeping the issue alive rather than facilitating a return to normalcy," Mr. Kumar said, claiming that "using students to advance extraneous or political agendas" was unacceptable and detrimental to their academic interests.
"The institute will extend full cooperation to the SIT and expects all concerned to respect the established legal process," the SRFTI registrar said.
The institute has been witnessing protests since September 27 following alleged attacks on students during an RSS-linked Akhil Bharatiya Grahak Panchayat event on the campus.

The stir intensified after a second alleged attack on October 4 during a rally by Bangiya Hindu Jagran Manch, with students organising sit-ins and raising concerns over their safety, privacy and freedom of movement.

articles.title: A nonagenarian from Virudhunagar on a mission to spread Gandhi’s message
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: By contributing articles to Tamil journals, A. Pitchai, 91, has been spreading the importance and relevance of Gandhian thought since his retirement from service in the State government

Middle-aged persons may be contemplating taking early retirement from their work, but in Tamil Nadu, a nonagenarian from Virudhunagar district is not only physically and mentally active but also continues to write Tamil articles and launch books.

By contributing articles to Tamil journals, A. Pitchai, 91, has been spreading the importance and relevance of Gandhian thought since his retirement from service in the State government. Recently, he brought out a Tamil book on Gandhian philosophy, a subject that is dear to his heart. He is working on yet another book on the topic.

Born in February 1935, Mr. Pitchai, who was the first Director of the State government’s exclusive unit for the welfare of persons with disabilities after it was separated from the Directorate of Social Welfare in 1992, received a Ph.D. from the University of Madras, at the age of 70, for his study on Tamil Nadu’s experiences in rehabilitation management of persons with disabilities. A recipient of the State government’s “best social worker award,” the scholar of Gandhian philosophy has been serving, in his individual capacity, persons with disabilities through an organisation (Speaker Chellapandian Charitable Trust) instituted in memory of his father-in-law.

His latest book, ‘Gandhi Ennum Aarparithaadum Sol’, published by Sandhya Publications, contains articles carried by Tamil newspaper Dinamani between September 2021 and January 2026. Recalling Gandhi’s momentous decision in Madurai to change his attire to a simple dhoti and shawl from the elaborate Gujarati attire on September 22, 1921, the author suggested that the day be observed as a ‘day of simplicity’ and that the Tamil Nadu government organise an event to mark the occasion.

Another piece talks of Gandhi’s favourite devotional song, Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye , and its composer, Narsinh Mehta of Gujarat. One of the articles, published in November 2022, captures the plight of the Porbandar house where Gandhi was born, and calls for the early reopening of the structure that remained closed ostensibly for repairs. Mr. Pitchai also echoes the concerns of fellow Gandhians over the Gujarat government’s plan to renovate the Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad and argues that in the name of redevelopment, the spirit and ethos of Gandhian simplicity should not be disturbed but preserved.
